result.rule: Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.

Respect event positions: a none intermediate event is catch-only in normal flow and never on a boundary; link events are intermediate-only, thrown and caught in pairs at the same process level, and a catching link has no incoming sequence flow; terminate is an end event only.
Use bpmn:task for atomic work when the execution mode is unspecified. A task contains no internal flow.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.

result.rule: When the description states that a process participant sends a request or information to an external party and describes that party returning information or otherwise responding: Model the external party as a separate participant pool, keep the sending and receiving work or events in the process participant’s own pool, and represent the exchanges with message flows.

When the description identifies a software system separate from the process’s own system and describes process interaction through it, such as initiating the process or receiving its results: Model that system as a separate participant pool, not as a lane in the process, and use message flows for the interactions between the pools.

When the description says an external participant sends information to an internal process, which then makes that information available through a user-facing interface: Model the incoming communication to a message-catching event in the internal process, and model making the information available through the interface as a separate internal activity; do not direct the external message to the interface.

When the description mentions an external party only as the recipient of a communication or as the source of a response or event, without describing that party’s own actions in the process: do not create a separate participant pool or message flows solely from that mention; add them only when the description establishes the party’s participation in the collaboration
